title: Statistics / Biostatistics
description: Develops practical statistical fluency for environmental and biological data: study design, uncertainty, inference, modeling, visualization, reproducible workflows, and responsible communication.

topics.title: Statistical Thinking for Environmental and Biological Data
topics.description: This opening topic frames statistics as a disciplined way to learn from variable, incomplete, and context-rich environmental and biological observations.

children.title: Statistical questions
children.description: Students learn to turn environmental questions into measurable variables and defensible analyses.

children.title: Variability and uncertainty
children.description: The point of statistics is not to remove variability but to describe and reason with it.

children.title: Causal and associational claims
children.description: Students learn why statistical association is not automatically cause.

topics.title: Data Types and Study Design
topics.description: Good analysis begins before data collection. This unit teaches students how design choices shape what conclusions are possible.

children.title: Data types and structure
children.description: Students learn to recognize the form of data before choosing methods.

children.title: Observational studies
children.description: Many environmental and health questions rely on observational evidence.

children.title: Experimental design
children.description: Experiments give stronger causal evidence when designed carefully.

topics.title: Data Management, Cleaning, and Reproducible Workflows
topics.description: World-class applied statistics includes the practical craft of making data trustworthy and analyses repeatable.

children.title: Data organization
children.description: Students learn tidy, documented data structures that support analysis.

children.title: Cleaning and validation
children.description: Students learn to detect data problems without quietly inventing results.

children.title: Reproducible analysis
children.description: Environmental decisions need analyses others can inspect and rerun.

topics.title: Descriptive Statistics and Visualization
topics.description: Descriptive work helps students see patterns, anomalies, and uncertainty before formal modeling.

children.title: Numerical summaries
children.description: Students learn compact ways to describe center, spread, and position.

children.title: Exploratory visualization
children.description: Graphs reveal distributional shape, group differences, and relationships.

children.title: Environmental visualization
children.description: Students connect statistical graphics to maps, time series, and monitoring data.

topics.title: Probability Foundations and Distributions
topics.description: Probability gives the mathematical language for uncertainty, sampling variation, and model-based inference.

children.title: Probability rules
children.description: Students learn the rules behind risk, dependence, and uncertainty.

children.title: Random variables
children.description: Random variables connect real measurements to probability models.

children.title: Core distributions
children.description: Students learn distributions that recur in biological and environmental analysis.

topics.title: Sampling, Estimation, and Environmental Monitoring
topics.description: Sampling design determines whether an estimate is useful for science, management, or policy.

children.title: Sampling strategies
children.description: Students compare designs for field and biological data collection.

children.title: Point estimates
children.description: Estimates summarize unknown population quantities from sample data.

children.title: Monitoring programs
children.description: Students learn how repeated data collection supports environmental decisions.

topics.title: Confidence Intervals and Uncertainty Quantification
topics.description: Confidence intervals teach students to communicate estimates with uncertainty instead of pretending one number is exact.

children.title: Interval estimation
children.description: Students learn what intervals do and do not mean.

children.title: Intervals for common quantities
children.description: Students practice intervals for means, proportions, and differences.

children.title: Uncertainty communication
children.description: Students learn to present uncertainty honestly to scientific and public audiences.

topics.title: Hypothesis Testing and Evidence
topics.description: Hypothesis tests formalize evidence against a reference claim, but they must be used with judgment.

children.title: Testing logic
children.description: Students learn the structure and limitations of null-hypothesis testing.

children.title: Common tests
children.description: Students apply tests for means, proportions, and paired designs.

children.title: Power and errors
children.description: Students learn that non-significant results are not the same as no effect.

children.title: Type I and Type II errors

topics.title: Correlation, Linear Regression, and Prediction
topics.description: Regression helps students describe relationships, adjust for predictors, and make cautious predictions.

children.title: Correlation
children.description: Students learn how to quantify association while respecting its limits.

children.title: Simple linear regression
children.description: Regression turns a relationship into an estimated model with uncertainty.

children.title: Diagnostics and prediction
children.description: Students learn to check whether a model is credible enough to use.

topics.title: Multiple Regression and Model Building
topics.description: Environmental and biological systems usually involve several interacting predictors, so students need a careful introduction to multivariable modeling.

children.title: Multiple predictors
children.description: Students learn how models can adjust for multiple variables at once.

children.title: Model selection and validation
children.description: Students learn that a model must be useful beyond the data used to fit it.

children.title: Interpretation in context
children.description: Students practice translating coefficients into environmental or biological meaning.

topics.title: ANOVA and Designed Experiments
topics.description: ANOVA connects experimental design to inference when comparing several groups or treatments.

children.title: One-way ANOVA
children.description: Students learn how to compare group means while controlling overall error.

children.title: Factorial designs
children.description: Factorial designs reveal interactions among treatments or environmental conditions.

children.title: Repeated and nested designs
children.description: Environmental data often contain structure that violates simple independence.

topics.title: Categorical Data and Risk Measures
topics.description: Biostatistics and environmental health often involve counts, proportions, disease status, exposure categories, and risk comparisons.

children.title: Contingency tables
children.description: Students learn to analyze relationships between categorical variables.

children.title: Risk and association measures
children.description: Risk measures turn counts into interpretable public-health evidence.

children.title: Logistic regression preview
children.description: Students see how binary outcomes can be modeled with predictors.

topics.title: Nonparametric and Robust Methods
topics.description: Not all data satisfy textbook assumptions. This unit gives students tools for skewed, ordinal, or outlier-prone data.

children.title: Rank-based methods
children.description: Students learn alternatives when normal-model assumptions are weak.

children.title: Robust summaries
children.description: Robust methods reduce sensitivity to extreme values.

children.title: Permutation and bootstrap ideas
children.description: Simulation-based methods make inference more intuitive and flexible.

topics.title: Time Series, Spatial Data, and Environmental Dependence
topics.description: Environmental data are often correlated in time and space, so students need to recognize dependence even in an introductory course.

children.title: Temporal dependence
children.description: Students learn why repeated measurements over time are not independent.

children.title: Spatial dependence
children.description: Nearby locations often resemble each other, affecting maps and inference.

children.title: Applied environmental examples
children.description: Students connect dependence to monitoring and prediction.

topics.title: Ethics, Equity, and Communication of Statistics
topics.description: Statistics affects environmental and health decisions, so students must communicate honestly and consider who is represented or harmed.

children.title: Ethical data practice
children.description: Students learn responsibility in data collection, analysis, and reporting.

children.title: Equity and representation
children.description: Sampling and modeling choices can hide or reveal environmental injustice.

children.title: Statistical communication
children.description: Students learn to explain results clearly without overstating certainty.

topics.title: Environmental Data Analysis Project
topics.description: The course culminates in an applied project where students move from question to data, analysis, interpretation, and communication.

children.title: Project design
children.description: Students define a question that can be answered with available environmental or biological data.

children.title: Analysis workflow
children.description: Students practice the full applied statistics process.

children.title: Reporting and reflection
children.description: Students produce a transparent report that connects results to context and uncertainty.
